security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences and Rust examples, including tokio::spawn and placeholder TLS filenames. The confirmed risks are all-interface listener examples, permissive CORS guidance, and full request logging guidance.

remediation.issue: Remote listener examples bind to all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Use 127.0.0.1 in starter examples. Show 0.0.0.0 only with TLS, authentication, and explicit exposure guidance.
Replace allow_origin(Any) with a concrete allowlist and explain separate development and production settings.

remediation.issue: Observability example logs full request data.
remediation.suggestion: Log method, request id, status, latency, and redacted metadata instead of the full request body.

content.value_statement: MCP servers need the right transport for local, web, and cloud deployments. This skill compares stdio, SSE, HTTP streaming, and custom options.
actual_capabilities: Compares stdio, SSE, HTTP streaming, and custom MCP transports.
Explains when each transport fits local, cloud, and web deployments.
Provides Rust examples for server setup, handlers, tests, and deployment.
Covers TLS, authentication, rate limiting, logging, and metrics guidance.
Helps design custom transports such as WebSocket-based transport layers.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not install or run MCP servers.
Examples need project-specific validation before production use.
It focuses on Rust MCP patterns more than other languages.
It does not replace a full security review for remote deployments.

use_cases.title: Select a transport for a new MCP server
use_cases.description: Compare local and remote deployment needs, then choose stdio, SSE, HTTP streaming, or a custom transport.

use_cases.title: Prepare a remote MCP service
use_cases.description: Plan HTTP or SSE hosting with authentication, TLS, rate limiting, and monitoring considerations.

use_cases.title: Review transport design choices
use_cases.description: Check whether an existing MCP server uses a transport that matches its clients, scale, and security needs.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a transport
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an MCP transport for my server. My clients are local desktop users, and I need simple setup.

prompt_templates.title: Compare deployment options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare stdio, SSE, and HTTP streaming for an MCP server behind a load balancer. Include security tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Review a transport implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my MCP transport design for production. Focus on authentication, TLS, rate limiting, logging, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a custom transport
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a custom MCP transport for constrained devices. Explain message framing, backpressure, retries, and observability.

output_examples.input: I need an MCP server for Claude Desktop on one machine.
output_examples.output: Recommended transport: stdio. It fits local subprocess use, keeps setup simple, and avoids exposing a network listener.

output_examples.input: I need a remote MCP server for several web clients.
output_examples.output: Recommended transport: HTTP streaming or SSE. Add TLS, authentication, rate limits, and restricted origins before production use.

output_examples.input: I need to test my transport layer before deployment.
output_examples.output: Suggested checks: message framing, error responses, disconnect handling, authentication failure paths, latency, and request logging safety.

best_practices: Start with the narrowest transport that supports your clients and deployment model.
Use TLS, authentication, and rate limiting for every remote MCP transport.
Test transport behavior separately from tool business logic.
anti_patterns: Do not expose a local development MCP server on all interfaces by default.
Do not use open CORS settings for authenticated remote MCP endpoints.
Do not log complete MCP requests when they may contain sensitive data.

faq.question: What transport should I use for Claude Desktop?
faq.answer: Use stdio for Claude Desktop because it runs the MCP server as a local subprocess.

faq.question: When should I use SSE?
faq.answer: Use SSE when remote clients need server-pushed events and your infrastructure supports long-lived HTTP connections.

faq.question: When should I use HTTP streaming?
faq.answer: Use HTTP streaming for web services, API gateways, load balancers, and standard cloud infrastructure.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and decision guidance that need project-specific review and hardening.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes bearer token checks and recommends authentication for remote transports.

faq.question: Can it help with custom transports?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines custom transport design and includes a WebSocket-oriented example structure.
